newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops arrest Jewish settler in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops arrest Jewish settler in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli troops on Wednesday detained a Jewish settler in Hebron who was among a group that tried to lay claim to Arab-owned shops in the centre of the West Bank town, witnesses and Israeli police said.
They said about 10 armed settlers were posting signs on a cluster of Arab-owned grocery and meat shops near Jewish enclaves in Hebron, but were stopped by some 200 Israeli troops and border police.
"This is the property of Jews in Hebron," the signs, printed in Hebrew and English, said.
Witnesses said one settler was detained. Other settlers tried unsuccessfully to block the path of a police vehicle carrying the detainee from the scene.
"A force came to the scene, they prevented the action and arrested one," a police spokesman said.

Hebron, a flashpoint of violence, is currently the focus of U.S.-sponsored negotiations between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation. The sides are trying to hammer out an agreement on a long-overdue Israeli handover of parts of the city to Palestinian self-rule.
About 400 settlers who live amidst 100,000 Arabs in heavily armed compounds in Hebron's centre staunchly oppose the planned pullback.
The Hebron settlers have grown increasingly restive as Israeli and PLO negotiators inched closer towards a deal.
PLO negotiator Jamil al-Tarifi, head of the civilian affairs committee in the Hebron talks, said on Wednesday both sides have agreed on a compromise on civilian issues.
He gave no details but Israeli media reported that the compromise would grant the Palestinian Authority some civil powers over the Jews of Hebron, a prospect the settlers reject.
